$comment: Source portfolio assessment for issue #9 Part 2. 'enabled' sources are implemented collectors used by the bounded PoC. No source here requires authentication, payment, or bypassing access controls. Assessed 2026-09-21.

classes.name: Hacker News comments (Algolia public API)
classes.access: Public JSON API https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1/search (no auth, documented)
classes.terms_notes: Public API intended for programmatic use; no key required. Be polite: bounded queries, identifying User-Agent.
classes.rate_limit: Not documented as hard; Algolia free tier tolerates low volume. Spike caps total requests per run.
classes.expected_signal: Medium-high: practitioners describe manual workflows, tooling gaps, re-keying in candid comments.
classes.expected_volume: Thousands of relevant comments across query families.

classes.name: Stack Exchange network (public API v2.3)
classes.access: Public API https://api.stackexchange.com/2.3 (no auth documented; 300 requests/day per IP without key)
classes.terms_notes: API terms allow read access; attribution required if republishing content. Spike stores short excerpts for audit only.
classes.rate_limit: 300 requests/day unauthenticated; backoff field in every response.
classes.expected_signal: Medium: business-tooling questions often describe data wrangling, exports, and workarounds; rotating sites reaches business users beyond Stack Overflow.
classes.expected_volume: Hundreds of matching excerpts per query family.

options.site_rotation: Query attempt i uses sites[i % len(sites)], so one family spreads across the network without extra HTTP requests. Question ids are only unique within a site, so item ids include the site.

classes.name: GitHub issues/discussions search (REST API)
classes.access: Public REST search API https://api.github.com/search/issues (no auth for low volume)
classes.terms_notes: Search API unauthenticated limit is low (10 req/min). Bounded to a few queries per run.
classes.expected_signal: Medium: integration gaps and manual workaround reports around business tooling.
classes.expected_volume: Hundreds of matches per query, mostly feature requests (lower-value class).

classes.name: Reddit public search JSON
classes.terms_notes: Public endpoints are rate-limited and may block datacenter IPs; blocking must not be bypassed.
classes.rate_limit: Undocumented for public JSON; aggressive blocking observed.
classes.observed: HTTP 403 Blocked from this network on 2026-09-21. Recorded as an access failure; no bypass attempted.

classes.name: Discourse communities (public /search.json)
classes.access: Public read endpoint https://<site>/search.json (no auth). Site list is configurable.
classes.terms_notes: Discourse instances are self-hosted and their terms vary. Only public read endpoints are used; no authentication and no private endpoints. Each site must be checked by the owner for terms/robots before it is added to options.sites.
classes.rate_limit: Instance-dependent; the spike's per-run request cap applies.
classes.expected_signal: Medium-high: buyer-side professional communities (accounting, legal, trades, operations) discuss manual workarounds and paid staff more than developer forums do.
classes.expected_volume: Tens to hundreds of matching posts per query family, depending on the site list.

options.site_rotation: Query attempt i uses sites[i % len(sites)], so one family spreads across communities without extra HTTP requests. Item ids include the site because topic ids are only unique within an instance.
options.note: Disabled until the owner approves specific sites. Add hostnames (e.g. 'community.example.org') to options.sites and set enabled true.

classes.name: Software review platforms (G2, Capterra, TrustRadius)
classes.access: Public HTML; no public API for review content.
classes.terms_notes: Robots/ToS restrict scraping; anti-bot controls common. NOT pursued beyond assessment in this spike.
classes.expected_signal: Medium-high (switching/dissatisfaction language) but access constraints make unattended collection unsafe.
classes.blocked_reason: ToS/robots and anti-bot controls; issue #9 forbids bypassing these. Would require licensed data feed or manual sampling.

classes.name: Vendor support/community threads (e.g. Salesforce Trailblazer, QBO community)
classes.access: Public HTML; each vendor has its own ToS and anti-bot posture.
classes.terms_notes: Public pages vary; several vendors block automated access. Not implemented generically.
classes.expected_signal: High: user-reported workarounds against a named incumbent.
classes.blocked_reason: Per-vendor ToS review required before any automated collection; deferred.

classes.name: Public job ads describing repetitive admin
classes.access: Aggregator APIs exist (e.g. Adzuna, Reed) but require free API keys/accounts.
classes.terms_notes: Creating accounts is not permitted in this spike; assessment only.
classes.expected_signal: Medium: ad text describes recurring manual admin tasks and named systems.
classes.blocked_reason: Requires account/API key creation, which issue #9 does not permit without approval.

classes.name: Public procurement/tender documents (Find a Tender, TED, USASpending)
classes.access: UK Find a Tender has an open API/OCDS feed; TED publishes OCDS datasets.
classes.terms_notes: Open government licences (OGL). Feasible but documents are long and signal is indirect.
classes.expected_signal: Low-medium: reveals spend on manual/off-system processes only indirectly.
classes.blocked_reason: Deferred: high volume/low precision for a first bounded PoC; candidate for rotation later.

classes.name: Government manual workflow instructions (GOV.UK guidance, HMRC manuals)
classes.terms_notes: Open licence; no anti-bot posture for guidance pages.
classes.expected_signal: Medium: official instructions that mandate manual steps or re-keying between systems.
classes.blocked_reason: Deferred to keep PoC bounded; good candidate for query-family rotation.

classes.name: Professional/trade-body discussion (e.g. AccountingWEB, UKBF, LRG forums)
classes.access: Mixed; many require login to post but read is public; robots vary.
classes.terms_notes: Must respect robots.txt per site; several forums disallow crawling.
classes.expected_signal: High: narrow professional segments discussing tooling gaps.

classes.name: Integration/app marketplace listings and reviews (Shopify App Store, HubSpot, Zapier)
classes.terms_notes: Scraping restrictions apply; partner APIs require account.
classes.expected_signal: High: reviews state exactly where integrations are partial/read-only/manual.

classes.name: Public spreadsheets/templates/checklists (shared drives, template galleries)
classes.access: Mixed; often personal shares with unknown licence.
classes.terms_notes: Licence unclear for most; only clearly open sources acceptable.
classes.expected_signal: Medium: the existence of a spreadsheet workaround evidences manual process.

classes.name: Niche trade publications
classes.access: Public HTML, often paywalled for archive content.
classes.expected_signal: Low-medium: second-hand description of industry process pain.

query_families.$comment: Rotated across runs so we do not hammer the same queries. Each family is a list of literal search strings. Rewritten 2026-09-21: families now target spend, paid workarounds and named-system seams rather than generic complaint chatter, because widely-discussed pain is already monetised (see runs/20260921T122128Z-normal/issue-drafts-opportunity-quality.md).
a_manual_rekey: "copy and paste" between systems every week
b_tooling_gap: "there has to be a better way" admin
d_paid_workaround: "we pay a" virtual assistant data entry
